description: A documentary producer must lock the festival and promotional release package for Under Neon Rain, including archival-image substitutions, required credits, trailer music, and online-use commitments, after the relevant production leads complete the standard clearance huddle.

shared_context.S1: Under Neon Rain is prepared for a festival premiere, a festival-hosted online screening, and a 30-second promotional trailer.
shared_context.S2: The current delivery draft includes a 14-second 1980 protest newsreel excerpt, a 22-second subway archive excerpt, and the music cue "Glass City" in both the documentary and trailer.
shared_context.S3: Mara makes the binding call on the final release and promotional package.
shared_context.S4: The production's normal clearance process is a final huddle in which rights, archive, and music leads report any restrictions before Mara locks the package.

PF1.text: During the final rights audit, Julian confirmed that the 1980 protest newsreel license permits one in-person festival screening only and prohibits online use; the online version must replace it with the public-domain still image "Marchers at Dawn." The clearance tracker still carries the earlier assumption that the newsreel was cleared for all formats.

PF2.text: Nia received the museum's signed permission for the 22-second subway excerpt, which permits worldwide online use only if the on-screen credit reads exactly "Courtesy of Metro Archive." She received the signed wording after the draft credits had already been circulated.

PF3.text: Owen confirmed with the composer that "Glass City" may remain in the documentary only with the exact end-credit wording "Music: Glass City — composed by Elena Vale" and may not be used in any trailer; the licensed replacement cue for the trailer is "Open Circuit." The music log has not yet been updated from the old combined-use plan.

acceptance_conditions: The online documentary must replace the protest newsreel with the public-domain still image "Marchers at Dawn."
The subway excerpt must remain included.
The subway excerpt must carry the exact museum credit.
The documentary may retain "Glass City" with the exact composer credit.
The trailer must use "Open Circuit" instead of "Glass City."
A restriction on online protest-newsreel use must be logged.
The museum credit must be logged in the final delivery notes.
The trailer music replacement must be logged.

content_checks.C6: decisions['documentary_end_credit'] == 'Music: Glass City — composed by Elena Vale'
content_checks.C7: any('newsreel' in c.get('detail', '') and ('online' in c.get('detail', '') or 'Online' in c.get('detail', '')) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any('Courtesy of Metro Archive' in c.get('detail', '') and ('credit' in c.get('detail', '') or 'Credit' in c.get('detail', '')) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any('Open Circuit' in c.get('detail', '') and ('trailer' in c.get('detail', '') or 'Trailer' in c.get('detail', '')) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The confirmed license restriction changes the online protest visual from the 1980 newsreel to the exact replacement still "Marchers at Dawn" and requires an online-use restriction commitment.
The signed museum permission establishes that the subway excerpt can remain only with the exact credit "Courtesy of Metro Archive," changing both the retained excerpt and the draft-credit correction.
The composer confirmation permits "Glass City" in the documentary only with the exact Elena Vale credit and forces the trailer to use "Open Circuit" with a replacement commitment.
